description: Markets in Financial Instruments Directive II. Harmonises rules for investment firms, trading venues, and market infrastructure across the EU. Effective from January 2018. Key AML/FCP intersection: organisational requirements, governance, transaction reporting.
Markets in Financial Instruments Regulation. Directly applicable rules on transparency and reporting for securities, derivatives, and structured finance products. Companion regulation to MiFID II.
Regulation prohibiting insider dealing, market manipulation, and unlawful disclosure of inside information. STR obligation under MAR Art.16 overlaps with AML SAR requirements for investment firms.

Legal person whose regular occupation is the provision of investment services to third parties and/or the performance of investment activities. Investment firms are obliged entities under AMLR. Regulated under MiFID II authorisation framework.

A multilateral system operated by a market operator, which brings together or facilitates the bringing together of multiple third-party buying and selling interests in financial instruments. Highest level of trading venue in MiFID II hierarchy.

A multilateral system operated by an investment firm or market operator that brings together multiple third-party buying and selling interests in financial instruments. Less regulated than RM. Examples: Nasdaq Nordic alternative markets.

A multilateral system for non-equity instruments (bonds, derivatives, structured finance products). Operator has discretion in matching orders. Introduced by MiFID II to capture formerly unregulated trading venues.

Investment firm that deals on own account when executing client orders outside a regulated market, MTF, or OTF on an organised, frequent, systematic, and substantial basis. Subject to transparency requirements under MiFIR.

Obligation on investment firms to take all sufficient steps to obtain the best possible result for clients when executing orders. Considers price, costs, speed, likelihood of execution and settlement, size, and nature. Must have and publish execution policy.

Investment firms must assess suitability (for advisory and portfolio management) and appropriateness (for execution-only) of products for clients. Suitability assessment gathers information on investment objectives, financial situation, and knowledge/experience.

canonical_name: MiFID II Art. 16 — Organisational Requirements (AML Link)
description: MiFID II Art. 16 requires investment firms to establish adequate policies and procedures to detect risks of non-compliance with obligations including AML/CFT obligations. Firms must ensure compliance with all applicable law including AMLR. Senior management accountability for compliance framework.

Investment firms must report complete and accurate details of transactions in financial instruments to national competent authorities. Reports include client LEI/ID, instrument details, price, quantity, venue, and timestamp. Used for market surveillance and AML analysis.

Market participants must report suspicious transactions or orders that may constitute insider dealing, market manipulation, or attempt thereof, to competent authorities. STR under MAR and SAR under AMLR are separate but parallel obligations for investment firms.

canonical_name: MiFID II Art. 9 — Management Body Requirements
description: Requirements for the management body of investment firms: sufficient time commitment, adequate collective knowledge, avoid conflicts of interest. Interacts with EBA Fit & Proper guidelines and AML governance requirements.

Firms engaging in algorithmic trading must have effective systems and risk controls, kill switches, and market-making obligations. Algorithmic trading creates new ML/TF typologies including layering, spoofing, and wash trading — cross-reference to MAR.

20-character ISO 17442 identifier for legal entities engaging in financial transactions. Mandatory in MiFIR transaction reporting. Also used in TFR Travel Rule and beneficial ownership reporting. Managed by GLEIF.

Instruments covered by MiFID II: transferable securities, money market instruments, units in collective investment undertakings, derivative instruments, emission allowances. Scope determines whether MiFID II or AMLR obligations apply.

Clients deemed to possess the experience, knowledge and expertise to make their own investment decisions. Credit institutions, investment firms, insurance companies, pension funds, and large corporates are per se professional clients.

Client who is not a professional client. Subject to highest level of protection under MiFID II. Investment firms have more extensive obligations for retail clients including suitability reports, costs/charges disclosure, and appropriateness assessment.

Investment firms are obliged entities under AMLR in addition to MiFID II. CDD under AMLR supplements MiFID II client classification. Dual reporting: MAR STR (Art.16) + AML SAR (AMLR Art.69). MiFID II organisational requirements reference AML compliance.

Investment firms subject to both MiFID II conduct of business requirements and MAR market abuse prohibitions. Transaction reporting (MiFIR Art.26) used for market abuse surveillance. Layering/spoofing under MAR overlaps with AML transaction monitoring.

Investment firms subject to DORA digital operational resilience requirements in addition to MiFID II. DORA applies to investment firms from 17 January 2025. Trading system resilience, ICT risk management, and incident reporting.

Obligation to report all transactions in MiFIR-scope instruments to an ARM (Approved Reporting Mechanism) or directly to NCA within T+1. Reports contain 65 fields. Used by regulators for AML pattern analysis in addition to market surveillance.

Process for filing suspicious transaction reports under MAR Art.16: assess whether suspicious; prepare STR using prescribed form; file with national competent authority (FI in Sweden, FIN-FSA in Finland, etc.). Time limit: as soon as reasonably practicable.

canonical_name: MiFID II Product Governance (MiFID II Art. 16/24)
description: Manufacturers and distributors must ensure products are designed with specific target markets in mind, and that distribution strategies align with target markets. Annual product review required. AML/ML-risk considerations in product design.

canonical_name: ESMA — European Securities and Markets Authority
description: EU-level supervisory authority for securities markets. Issues technical standards, guidelines, and Q&As on MiFID II/MiFIR implementation. Coordinates NCAs. Does not directly supervise investment firms (national supervisors do).

European Commission legislative proposals to amend MiFID II and MiFIR, focused on: equity market structure reform, transparency improvements, data consolidation (consolidated tape), and enhanced retail investor protection. In legislative process as of 2024.

Crypto-assets that are financial instruments fall under MiFID II (e.g., security tokens). Crypto-assets that are NOT financial instruments fall under MiCA. The boundary is critical for determining applicable AML regime (AMLR applies to both CASPs and investment firms).
